narrative.overview:
ISOFT Desk is a shell, not a skin. It replaces the Frappe v13 desk's navigation and module pages with the polish users already know from Odoo 17, Linear, Stripe Dashboard and ERPNext v15: a theme-following sidebar on the left, a slim white top bar, and module pages that answer "what is waiting for me in this company" before anything else. The people using it are accounting, sales, stock and management staff on 1366x768 laptops, working in Portuguese or English. They arrive with a job, do it and leave. Density is moderate (13px body, 30 to 34px rows), and every surface is flat, white or slate, and separated by 1px tinted rules.

The world is quiet so that state can be loud. ISOFT cyan-blue is the only accent. It marks where you are, the primary action, focus and links. Green, amber and red appear only when a count means something needs attention. The v13 desk's cyan-topped card grid, star watermark and flat 20-item module list are removed on purpose.

The scope is deliberately narrow. Everything lives under `body.isd-on`, so a user outside the pilot, or a site with the app switched off, sees the standard desk unchanged. Lists, forms and reports keep core styling inside the shell. The only changes there are the accent on the primary button and, on forms, the collapsed rail with the core left column hidden.

Two surfaces sit before the shell and follow different rules. The login page is the incumbent core "vault" (two doors, module chips wired into an authentication core, the card at the seam), and core's dark vault is its design, not this app's. The app only adds a light recolouring of it, picked from the theme this browser last used on the desk. The loading screen (core's splash and the post-login boot cover) is drawn from the vault interior's own recipe, "ISOFT ERP" over "ENTERPRISE CORE · ONLINE" on the gridded core ground with its breathing glow, so after login the room the doors open onto simply stays on screen until the desk is ready: one screen, not two. Both paint before the shell exists, so they carry literal colours from this palette instead of the `--isd-*` tokens.
keyCharacteristics: Theme-following sidebar: a white panel with a 1px rule in light mode, deep slate in dark mode.
One accent, the ISOFT ERP logo's blue, in three strengths: a fill, a line and a text shade. Semantic colours carry state only.
Inter with tabular figures. Counts are large, and labels sit below them.
6px radii everywhere, 8px on menus. Menus and popovers are the only things with a shadow.
Every top-bar menu (Help, user, notifications, search results, the ISOFT applications launcher) sits on the desk's own surface, rule and shadow.
Fully scoped (`body.isd-on`). Core lists, forms and reports are not restyled.
The login vault opens in the browser's last desk theme; the light vault is a recolour, never a relayout.
Every load shows the vault interior, light or dark, in the desk theme the server rendered.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Inside the desk shell, ISOFT blue is the only hue that is not about state. A second brand colour, a gradient or a coloured section header does not belong there. The login vault and the loading screen are blue worlds too: their glow hues are blues from the same family, never a second hue. The one exception is the applications launcher's app icon tones: each tone names an app, so they keep their own hue while everything around them takes the desk tokens.

rules.name: The Fill, Line, Text Rule
rules.body: Each accent job has its own shade. Fills carry white ink (Logo Blue, about 4.8:1). Lines, borders, focus outlines and chart series use Logo Blue Bright, which holds 3:1 against the surface but is too light for text. Text uses the text shade (Logo Blue in light mode, Sky Link Blue in dark mode). Never set text in the line shade, and never use the fill shade for hairlines.

rules.name: The Vault Is Core's Rule
rules.body: The dark vault (core `login.scss` and `www/login.html`) is the incumbent design and stays where it is. This app only recolours it, under `html[data-isd-login="light"]`. Doors, chips, traces, core and card keep core's geometry, motion and gradients, and the light variant swaps their colours one for one. The single change that reaches both themes is a repair: core's breathing keyframes drop the glow's centring translate, so the app re-runs the same breath (`isd-vi-breathe`, 3.6s, opacity 0.55 to 0.9, scale 1 to 1.12) with the translate kept, and the glow sits centred on the title as core intended.

rules.name: The Colour Is State Rule
rules.body: A tile count turns red or amber only when its definition carries a tone and the count is above zero. A zero count goes faint, never green. Charts draw series 1 in Logo Blue Bright and further series in Ink Faint and Rule Strong, with no area fill.

rules.name: The Names Read As Names Rule
rules.body: Some core translations start in lowercase ("cotação"). Tile labels, DocType lines, quick links, index links and index headings capitalise their first letter, through CSS `::first-letter` or, for New buttons, in JS.

rules.name: The Own Context Rule
rules.body: Every interface string the app adds is translated with context "ISOFT Desk" (`__(text, replace, "ISOFT Desk")`), so it never overrides another app's translation of the same English word. Labels that belong to core (DocType names, workspace labels) use plain `__()`.

rules.name: The Two Lines Rule
rules.body: Sidebar labels wrap to at most two lines and never truncate to one. Long Portuguese names stay readable.

rules.name: The Only Menus Float Rule
rules.body: In the desk shell, a surface gets a shadow only if it floats over other content and closes again. Tiles, the top bar and the sidebar stay shadowless. The login vault is outside the shell and keeps the glow and lift that core's vault is built from, recoloured.

dos: Do scope every selector under `body.isd-on` (or the `.isd-` shell elements it creates), so switching the app off restores the standard desk. Two documented exceptions: the light vault (`html[data-isd-login="light"]`, set only while the app is enabled) and the loading screen (html-level, site-wide, because it paints before boot).

Do use the `--isd-*` custom properties, never literal hex, so light and dark both follow the desk theme. The login and loading-screen stylesheets are the exception: the `--isd-*` tokens are not loaded there, so they use literal values from the Login Surface palette or their own `--isd-core-*` properties.
Do settle the login theme before first paint (remembered desk theme, then the OS preference), so the vault never flashes the other variant.

Do keep the loading screen identical to the vault interior it continues (title, subtitle, grid, glow and ground), so the hand-off from the doors is invisible. Under reduced motion the glow holds still.
Do keep the logo blue for where-you-are, the primary action, focus and links, and pick its shade by job: fill, line or text. Nothing else is blue.
Do colour a count only through a definition's tone, and only when it is above zero.
Do translate added strings with context "ISOFT Desk".
Do hide the desk sidebar on any page that draws its own fixed sidebar, and add the route to the hidden list instead of restyling the page.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion` for the chevron, drawer and skeleton. The shared ease is `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`.
donts: Don't restyle core lists, forms or reports inside the shell. Only the primary-button accent and the form full-width rule reach them.
Don't list Isoft app pages in the sidebar. They live in the applications launcher.
Don't bring back the v13 cyan-topped card grid, the star watermark or a flat module list.
Don't add shadows to tiles, cards, the top bar or the sidebar. Only floating menus and tooltips cast one.
Don't give other apps' navbar buttons or menus their own colours inside the shell. The launcher's app icon tones are the only hues kept, because each names an app.
Don't fill chart areas or use more than one accent-coloured series.

Don't restyle the dark vault from this app, or move, resize or re-animate any part of the vault in the light variant. Change colours only. The glow-centring repair (same breath, translate kept) is the one change that reaches both vaults.
Don't draw an outline or ring on a clicked sidebar or menu control. Keyboard focus shows as the hover background.
